newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel, Dassault in bid for Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel, Dassault in bid for Thomson-CSF.

text.p: French industrial group Alcatel Alsthom said on Wednesday that it had made a joint offer with Dassault Industries for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF.
"Alcatel Alsthom and Dassault Industries have made a joint offer for Thomson-CSF," an Alcatel spokesman told Reuter.
Lagardere said separately it also had bid for Thomson-CSF.

Alcatel Alsthom and Dassault Industries said in a joint statement they were committed to increasing the size of Thomson-CSF "by close to 50 percent to create a world leader in defence electronics as well as in the associated civil sectors".
"These positions could be further reinforced, if as Alcatel Alsthom and Dassault Industries hope, Aerospatiale is authorised later on to participate in their industrial project."
Alcatel and Dassault said they could finance the acquisition from their own resources without compromising the future or using the resources of Thomson-CSF.

The first stage of the project would allow the regrouping in Thomson-CSF only of the main part of the space/defence electronics activities entirely controlled by French companies -- a regrouping already achieved in numerous countries, the companies said.

"Certain measures are being taken to follow and enlarge this regrouping at the European level, immediately after the first step has been accomplished... under such conditions which allow that unified French assets are fully valued," they said.

Alcatel Alsthom's 100 billion franc ($17.2 billion) capitalisation would allow Thomson-CSF to be supported by a "powerful and enduring group, who can assure its development in the same conditions as that of its international competitors", the said.

Thomson-CSF would remain a listed company, retaining its identity, while having access to one of the largest concentrations of research and development in the world, totalling 25 billion francs per year, resulting from the benefits of its civil-military synergies, they said.
A strategic and economic link could be established with the future Aerospatiale/Dassault Aviation, confirming their mutual position in the large civil and military programmes.

An attempt to sell the whole Thomson electronics group floundered last year when the independent privatisation commission rejected the sale of parent company Thomson SA to missiles-to-publishing conglomerate Lagardere for a symbolic one franc.
